title: EdgeBurst cartogram: performance digest
content:
Summary:
This note collects the initial microbench results for the EdgeBurst profile: short-lived high-concurrency spikes from geographically distributed edge POPs. Goal is to produce a compact cartogram (text charts, tables) for product review and to highlight where routing, prefetch, and compact quantization yield measurable dollar-per-p99 improvements.

Benchmark goal:
- Measure p50/p90/p99 latency and $/1k-token for a small chat model across three serving modes and three HW types under spike-shaped load (10s ramp, 30s peak, 60s decay).
- Capture transient penalties: cold-slot startup, KV-prefetch warmups, and fast-fallback routing.
- Produce cheap-to-read text visualizations for PM/SE review.

Environment & config:
- Model: rw-mini-6b (base) and rw-mini-6b-compact (8-bit+per-channel compaction)
- HW: A100 (40GB), T4 (16GB), Edge-Cloud-GPU (latency-optimized 80GB equivalent)
- Serving modes: multiplexed smallbatch, dedicated slot (pin), and prewarmed pool (warm)
- Network sim: added 20–80ms RTT variance per POP, simulating edge backhaul jitter
- Workload shape: 10s ramp to N=250 concurrent sessions, 30s peak, 60s decay, synthetic token lengths: prompt 30 tokens, response 60 tokens average
- Key knobs: KV-prefetch=on/off, batch-window=5ms/10ms/20ms, quantized-run=on/off

Measurement notes (what we report):
- p50/p90/p99 latency (tail measured at client-observed level)
- TCO metric: $ per 1k tokens (in hosting config, amortized across instance minutes)
- Cold penalty: measured on first-request-to-warm in prewarm vs on-demand slots
- Hit-rate proxy: KV cache warm-hit fraction per session

Results (compact table):
Format: MODE | HW | MODEL | p50(ms) | p90(ms) | p99(ms) | $/1k toks | cold-penalty(ms) | kv-hit
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
warm   | A100 | base    | 120     | 220     | 420     | $6.5      | 40                | 0.85
warm   | A100 | compact | 130     | 240     | 460     | $5.2      | 35                | 0.88
smallb | A100 | base    | 140     | 280     | 780     | $5.0      | 95                | 0.62
smallb | T4   | compact | 210     | 420     | 1100    | $3.7      | 160               | 0.57
pin    | Edge | compact | 160     | 300     | 520     | $7.2      | 30                | 0.90

Ascii cartogram — peak p99 vs $/1k (horizontal bars):
Legend: p99(ms) -> '|', $/1k (normalized) -> '#' (longer means cheaper per token)
A100-warm-base   p99:420  |||||||||||||||||  $:6.5  ##
A100-warm-compact p99:460  ||||||||||||||||||  $:5.2  ####
A100-smallb-base p99:780  ||||||||||||||||||||||||||||  $:5.0  #####
T4-smallb-compact p99:1100 |||||||||||||||||||||||||||||||||||| $:3.7  ########
Edge-pin-compact p99:520 |||||||||||||||||||||||  $:7.2  #
(Interpretation: narrower p99 = better latency; more # = lower cost per token)

Key observations:
1) Compact quantization gives clear $/1k improvements vs base model on all HW — 15–35% cheaper depending on HW. The compact variant often slightly increases p99 in warm mode but reduces $s significantly.
2) Smallbatch multiplexing reduces $/1k on amortized throughput but increases tail latency heavily during sharp spikes — p99 blowups were 2–3x vs warm prewarmed pools on A100.
3) Edge-pin (dedicated pinned slot at POP) delivers stable p99 and highest KV hit rates but at higher $/1k (lower multiplexing efficiency). Good fit for strict SLO customers.
4) Cold penalties dominate first-10s of the spike in smallbatch mode; prewarm pool minimized that window.
5) KV-prefetch increases hit fraction ~20–30% during session sequences and lowers effective p99 by ~50–80ms (depends on batch-window).

Tradeoff sketches (short):
- If SLO p99 < 500ms required: favor warm prewarmed or pin at edge with compact quantization. Expect 10–20% extra $ compared to best-effort multiplexing.
- If cost minimization is primary and p99 up to ~1s is tolerable: smallbatch on T4 with compact quant yields lowest $/1k. Acceptable for asynchronous or retry-friendly flows.

Open questions / unknowns (for discussion):
- How does multi-POP fanout affect end-to-end p99 when requests are routed to nearest POP with fallback? Need a DAG-level sim. (See JIRA-ENG-7321)
- Snapshot here uses rw-mini-6b; port to rw-large-16b may change tiling/batch-window optimal points. Quick follow-up run requested.
- Need more telemetry to separate network vs server decode tails — current client-observed p99 conflates both.

Next steps / action items:
- [Marco] run a 3x repeat with longer decay (300s) to measure sustained microburst behaviors (due: 2029-06-18)
- [Jinsoo] add network-split telemetry to isolate backhaul jitter (due: 2029-06-20)
- [Aisha] prepare slide one-pager for product review (two charts: p99 vs $/1k and cold-penalty distro) by 2029-06-21
- [Lina] prototype routing policy that prefers prewarm for SLO-tagged requests, then quantize aggressively for fallback; quick A/B by 2029-06-25

Appendix: quick methodology notes:
- All cost numbers use current internal instance cost rate (June 2029) and amortize instance-minutes across tokens generated in the test window. Does not include storage or network egress.
- pXX measured at client-observed wall time (includes network RTT). For server-only tail, subtract median RTT estimate (provided in next iteration).

Rough links / refs: JIRA-ENG-7321 (routing-sim), confluence: EDGE-Perf-cartogram, github PR: benchmarks/pull/184

Notes to self (scratchpad):
- Consider adding microcdf plots next iteration (ascii buckets).
- Double-check pricing weights for prewarm CPU overhead on Edge-pin rows — current calc may undercount OS overhead by ~5%.
